Bylaw-2018
Computer Engineering and Software Systems Program (CESS)
1. Program mission
“The CESS program mission is to provide high quality education in the field of computer engineering and software systems to contribute to the preparation of a distinguished graduate capable of staying up-to-date with the global technological development in the field of computer engineering and software systems, capable of meeting the needs of the local, regional and international market, and able to conduct scientific and applied research. The program’s mission
is realized through the continuous development of the program.”
The systematic development of high-quality software systems that are concerned with quality, cost, time, and a number of other requirements, demands well-qualified engineers in this field. Software engineering is one of the most promising fields in engineering and is considered an important milestone in the ever-growing information technology sector.
Therefore, the main objective of this program is to graduate highly qualified engineers in the fields of computer engineering and software industry. This program focuses on modern methodologies in software industry that represents an important sector of the national economy. In this program, students study a variety of courses that complement each other to produce a world-class qualified engineer.

2. Program aims
By successfully completing the Computer Engineering and Software Systems program at the Faculty of Engineering,
Ain Shams University, the graduate will be able to:
PA 1. Apply knowledge of mathematics, science and engineering concepts to the solution of computer and software engineering problems.
PA 2. Identify, formulate, and solve fundamental engineering problems.
PA 3. Use the techniques, skills, and engineering tools, necessary for engineering practice and project management.
PA 4. Demonstrate knowledge of contemporary engineering issues.
PA 5. Design computer/software systems; components and processes to meet the requirements specifications within realistic constraints.
PA 6. Design and conduct analysis process and experiments as well as analyze and interpret data.
PA 7. Use current techniques, skills, and tools necessary for computing practices to specify, analyze, design, implement, verify, validate, and evolve computer- and software- based systems.
PA 8. Recognize the information requirements of various business activities on both operational and decision-making levels.
PA 9. Tackle business problems using system analysis tools and techniques.
PA 10.

PA 10. Manage projects related to computer and software engineering in diverse fields of applications.
PA 11. Implement the different phases of the computer and software systems development life-cycle, procurement and installation of hardware, software analysis, design, validation, verification, and maintenance, data manipulation and system operations.

3. Graduate attributes
To achieve the program mission and aims, program graduates should be able to:
GA 1- Master a wide spectrum of engineering knowledge and specialized skills and can apply acquired knowledge using theories and abstract thinking in real life situations.
GA 2- Apply analytic critical and systemic thinking to identify, diagnose and solve engineering problems with a wide range of complexity and variation.
GA 3- Behave professionally and adhere to engineering ethics and standards.
GA 4- Work in and lead a heterogeneous team of professionals from different engineering specialties and assume responsibility for own and team performance.
GA 5- Recognize his/her role in promoting the engineering field and contribute in the development of the profession and the community.
GA 6- Value the importance of the environment, both physical and natural, and work to promote sustainability principles.

4. Program Career Prospects
The graduate of this program will establish technical leadership in the area of computer engineering and software
systems. In addition to his contributions as a professional engineer who is able to participate and cooperate productively
in his respective fields. The skills of the graduates of this program that include computer engineering, software engineering, distributed and mobile computing, embedded systems, computer security, multimedia systems, data science, and others, will lead to high-level positions in leading the engineering projects in these areas. Therefore, this program will meet the increasing demand for this specialization to meet the market needs at the national, regional, and international levels.
The program qualifies graduates to work as computer and software engineers. The graduate can be specialized in one of the following four concentrations (fields):

rnational levels.
The program qualifies graduates to work as computer and software engineers. The graduate can be specialized in one of the following four concentrations (fields):
1. Multimedia and Computer Graphics: This concentration prepares the graduate to work in the
field of graphics software development including image processing, vision, computer animation, and games development.
2. Distributed and Mobile Computing: This concentration prepares the graduate to work in the field
of distributed systems and networking including cloud computing, wireless and mobile networks, digital forensics, IOT, and parallel computing.
3. Software Product Lines: This concentration prepares the graduate to work as a full-fledged
software engineer who deeply understands all software development processes and aspects including financial, managerial, and design, security, and performance aspects.
4. Data Science: This concentration prepares the graduate to work as a data scientist by covering a
wide range of topics including big-data, machine learning, deep learning, and various application such as bioinformatics and business intelligence.

5. Agreements with another University
The program is in partnership with the University of East London (UEL), one of the leading modern Universities in the United Kingdom for Engineering and Computing. The Graduates are eligible for the B.Sc. Computer
Engineering and Software Systems dual award from Ain Shams University and the University of East London.
Both institutions work together to ensure the quality and standards of the program on which the students are
registered. Students are allowed to study one semester or more at UEL with a 10% reduction in the UK tuition fees.
6. Program admission requirements
• Students with Egyptian Secondary education or equivalent certificate with major in Mathematics and/or
equivalent diplomas may apply for admission/enrolment in the Credit Hours Engineering Programs after being accepted in the Faculty of Engineering (ASU) based on the rules yearly set by the Higher Council of
Universities.
•
The official teaching Language is English, and the Faculty of Engineering will ascertain the student's English
Language proficiency. Textbooks, assignments, and examinations are all in English.

7.6 Program Study Duration
•
The minimum allowed study duration is nine main semesters.
•
The maximum allowed study duration is twenty main semesters (ten years), which does not include frozen semesters for reasons accepted by the Faculty of Engineering Council, after which the student is dismissed from the programs.
7.7 Degree Awarding Requirements
•
To obtain the Bachelor of Science Degree in Computer Engineering and Software Systems, the student must successfully complete the required Credit Hours in the program with a GPA at graduation of at least
2.0.
•
The student must pass all zero-credit courses in the Program.
•
A graduation project is an essential part of the program requirements for graduation. The graduation project may be completed over two successive semesters, as per the program requirement, and the student will not graduate unless he fulfils the project pass requirements. The student must earn at least 130 Credit
Hours to register for the graduation project. If the project is divided along two semesters, the student must register them in their order.
•
The student must perform Field Training for 12 weeks during his study duration.
•
The student can study a number of courses in another University which has a cooperation agreement with
Ain Shams University regarding the transfer of Credits. This requires prior approval from the Faculty of

er of courses in another University which has a cooperation agreement with
Ain Shams University regarding the transfer of Credits. This requires prior approval from the Faculty of
Engineering, Ain Shams University. The Credit Hours of these courses are included in the student's graduation requirements, provided that the total Credit Hours of these courses do not exceed 68 Credit
Hours.
7.8 Field Training
•
The student must perform Field Training for 12 weeks in an industrial or service facility related to the student's program and must be under the full supervision of the faculty. It is also possible to perform the training inside the faculty in a similar environment.
•
The training follow-up will be handled by the academic advisor assigned by the Program Steering
Committee.
•
The training is divided into periods of 4 weeks at the end of the first, second, and third levels. (Can be in the fourth level as well – open during the semester)

Major Programs (144 CH)
The 11 Inter-Disciplinary Major Programs are:
•Materials Engineering Program.
•Manufacturing Engineering Program.

•Building Engineering Program.

Minor Programs (around 18 CH)
Students can choose from 38 minor programs to complement their major studies.
•Distribution by Department:
•Mechanical Engineering: 11 Minors.
•Architectural Engineering: 6 Minors.
•Electrical Engineering: 10 Minors.
•Civil Engineering: 11 Minors

Academic System & Duration
•A student moves to the next level after completing 25% (36 credit hours) of the program requirements.
•Levels are defined based on the percentage of completed credits:
•Level 1: 0% to <25%.
•Level 2: 25% to <50%.
•Level 3: 50% to <75%.
•Level 4: 75% to <100%.
•Program Duration
•Minimum: Eight main semesters.
•Maximum: Eight academic years (excluding approved enrollment suspensions). An additional academic year is granted for students enrolled in a minor program

University Requirements (11 CHs)

Course Registration Rules
The number of credits a student can register for depends on their cumulative GPA.
•Main Semesters (Fall/Spring):
•GPA ≥ 3.0: Up to 21 credit hours (or 8 courses, whichever is greater).
•2.0 ≤ GPA < 3.0: Up to 18 credit hours (or 7 courses, whichever is greater).
•GPA < 2.0: Up to 14 credit hours (or 5 courses, whichever is greater).
•Summer Semester:
•GPA ≥ 3.0: Up to 9 credit hours (or 3 courses, whichever is greater).
•GPA < 3.0: Up to 8 credit hours (or 2 courses, whichever is greater).

Graduation Requirements
To be awarded a Bachelor of Science in Engineering, a student must:
•Successfully complete the required number of credit hours for their major program.
•Achieve a final cumulative GPA of at least 2.0.
•Pass all mandatory courses with zero (0) credit hours.
•Successfully complete the graduation project. Students must pass at least
70%(101 hours) of the program's total credit hours to register for the project.
•Complete the required field training ( 8 weeks)

Field Training
Field training is a mandatory component of the degree.
•Duration: 8 weeks in a relevant industrial or service facility.
•Timing: The training is divided into two parts: 4 weeks at the end of the second level and 4 weeks at the end of the third level.
• Training can be started after passing 26 CHs of the freshman level, provided
that the duration for the training does not exceed two weeks
• In any case, training for a 6-week period at any level is permitted only once
during the study period

Academic Standing
•Academic Warning
•A student is placed on academic warning if their cumulative GPA drops below
2.0 in any main semester.
•Dismissal from Study
•A student may be dismissed for reasons including:
•Having a cumulative GPA below 1.0 after the first three main semesters.
•Having a cumulative GPA below 2.0 for six consecutive main semesters.
•Failing to meet graduation requirements within the maximum study period.

Selecting Your Elective Track
• Students must complete 7 elective courses (21 credit hours).
• At least 5 courses must be chosen from one concentration.
• Four Tracks are available to guide specialization.

Track 1 Multimedia and Computer Graphics
• Focus: Graphics software development.
• Topics include:
• Image processing
• Computer vision
• Animation
• Games development
• Prepares graduates for roles in graphics & visual computing industries.

Track 2 Distributed and Mobile Computing
• Focus: Distributed systems and networking.
• Topics include:
• Cloud computing
• Wireless & mobile networks
• Internet of Things (IoT)
• Digital forensics
• Parallel computing
• Prepares graduates for careers in networking, IoT, and cloud-based solutions.

Track 3 Software Product Lines
• Focus: Advanced software engineering.
• Topics include:
• Software development processes
• Financial and managerial aspects
• System design and architecture
• Security & performance
• Prepares graduates to be well-rounded software engineers.

Track 4 Data Science
• Focus: Data-driven decision making.
• Topics include:
• Big data analytics
• Machine learning & deep learning
• Bioinformatics applications
• Business intelligence
• Prepares graduates for careers as data scientists and AI specialists

Dual Degree: Ain Shams University × University of East London (UEL)
• Students receive two B.Sc. awards: one from ASU and one from UEL upon completion of the program
requirements in Egypt.
• Travel is not required; optional study in London can be arranged with fee reductions on the UEL
campus if chosen
• Four-year study plan in Egypt following the 2023 bylaw/approved plan; UEL module coordination is
embedded
• Students must fulfil admission requirements (e.g., IELTS 5.5 overall, with minimum 5.5 in each
component)

UEL Academic Levels
• UEL program contains 4 levels: Level 3 (CN3XXX) → Level 6 (CN6XXX)
• Equivalent to the four years at ASU
• Each level = 6 modules
• Each UEL module corresponds to 1 or 2 ASU courses

UEL Progression Rules
Level 3: must pass all 6 modules to progress
Higher levels (4–6):
• Must pass at least 5 modules
• 1 failed module can be carried over to the next year

Module Registration Rules
• You cannot register for a UEL module in a higher level
• If a UEL module is offered in Fall and appears in the CAIE course tree as Fall, you must register for it in Fall
No guarantee it will be re-offered in Spring or Summer
• If you fail a UEL module in:
•
First sit exam
•
Re-sit exam
→ You must re-register the module within the same academic year or the next year to avoid dismissal from UEL
• Failing again (including re-sit) will result in dismissal from the UEL program

Module Registration Rules (Cont.)
Conclusion:
A student has a maximum of four opportunities to pass a module:
•
First registration – includes first sit and resit.
•
Second registration (within the same academic year or the following year at the latest) – includes first sit and resit.
If the student fails after these four attempts, they will be dismissed from the UEL program.

UEL Advanced Entry Rule
Advanced entry to higher levels is possible only if:
• All lower-level modules are completed

Assessment & Grading Criteria and the Difference Between
ASU Courses and UEL Modules.

Assessment & Grading (ASU Courses)
Grading covers all course components:
• Midterm exam
• Final exam
• Quizzes
• Major task/project
• Lab exam (if applicable)
Pass mark: 60% minimum
If failed
→ student must repeat the course in a future semester

Assessment & Grading (UEL Modules)
Grading covers fewer components (no quizzes, no midterm)
Pass mark: 40% minimum
If failed
→ student can enter a Resit Exam immediately after final exams
Portfolio submission required for any course included in a UEL module
(includes major tasks)

Special Cases
•
In some cases, if you fail an ASU course, there is still a chance to pass the equivalent UEL module.
•
In other cases, if you fail an ASU course, you may pass the UEL module after entering the resit exam.
•
In very rare cases, you may fail the UEL module while passing the ASU course.
• Don’t worry – this is extremely rare.
• If this happens, you will be contacted by email with guidance.

Aim of Student’s Guidelines Booklet (SGB)
The main aim of the SGB is to set a clear view for the students regarding their coursework submissions and the appropriate submission process. In addition, the SGB clarifies to students various items such as: coursework assessment types, submission matrix, submission format, submission naming system and submission templates. Furthermore, SGB highlights the scanning guidelines for coursework submission and help request procedures (if needed). It is worth noting
that as part of dual degree requirements, all students’ submissions are reassessed by an
External Examiner (E.E.) from U.K. The E.E. has the authority to approve the marks, request change of mark or refuse the awarded mark.

1. Course Assessment Components
Course assessment consists of two types, namely “Coursework Assessment” and “Final
Examination”. The aim of the coursework assessment is to evaluate student’s performance during the semester. Coursework assessment represent the term work marks for the students and its weight varies according to the course specs and program bylaws. The Coursework Assessment consists of different assessment activities (specified in the course specifications) such as projects, reports, presentations, laboratory work, field measurements, marked assignments, midterm
examination, quizzes, pop quizzes, and any other activities as specified in the course specs.
By the end of the semester, all students are requested to submit a complete portfolio. This portfolio is a collection of all Coursework Assessment items evaluated during the semester. The portfolio is mainly a softcopy to be submitted online as will be explained later in this guide.
Plagiarism rules apply to all types of coursework assessments.

Plagiarism rules apply to all types of coursework assessments. The penalty of plagiarism can vary from failing the module and a mark of 0 will be recorded for all components, three courses, of assessment in the relevant module or the student can be suspended from his/her studies for the following academic year. For further details about plagiarism, student must refer to the student handbook.

The submission matrix highlights dates/weeks assigned for submitting various components within each course. In addition, it helps him/her to relate the various submissions within different courses in semester. Furthermore, it helps him/her to avoid any conflicts in submission dates. Accordingly, he/she can plan well the required submissions ahead.
The submission matrix specifies the following:
▪ Semester
▪ Course code
▪ Course name
▪ week

All course work components must be uploaded on IMS in a single PDF file and not in many files. A downloadable video to illustrate how to upload your portfolio on IMS is listed in the list of the downloadable links at the end of this file.
3-h. Student’s work Scanning Guidelines
The following are guidelines illustrating the required quality of scanned documents within the portfolio:
• Documents must be scanned from the original documents and not from photocopied copies.
• Scanned documents should be with high-quality and clear to read. Any words and numbers on
the document should be clear and readable, not blurry and without any glare.
• Poor-quality documents must be rejected.
• Documents must be scanned with a flatbed scanner and should appear flat, without any visible
folds or creases.
• Digital photocopies and scans from smartphone applications will not be accepted.
• Documents must be scanned at the original size. If the document is larger than A4 then the
document should be scanned in A4 sized portions without size reduction.
• Both sides of the document must be scanned.
• File size of a portfolio should not exceed 5 MB.

5-c. Useful Hints to effectively prepare for the IELTS exam.
The under mentioned sections are based on a previous experience. The below mentioned link can help the student be prepared with less expenses or require less time than the
IELTS preparation course which cost around 2200 EGP. However, students are free to choose the way the will prepare for their exam.
1. The IELTS 6 hours’ workshop (around 250 EGP)
This one-day workshop explains to you the different parts of the exam. It involves some practical tips for solving the exam. It also provides you with some practice material.
For more information:
https://www.britishcouncil.org.eg/en/exam/ielts/courses-resources/workshop
2. IELTS Simulator (around 350 EGP)
This session lasts for 3.5 hours. During this time, you undergo an IELTS exam like the one you will be taking on the test day. You do not receive a band score after the simulator.
Instead, you receive detailed feedback within 7 working days that helps you better prepare for the real test.
